evidence.claim: A mountain lake and park built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
evidence.quote: It is one of the six original Virginia state parks, built in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.claim: A mountain lake and park built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
evidence.quote: Douthat State Park is a state park located in the Allegheny Mountains in Virginia.

evidence.claim: Douthat State Park occupies 4,545 acres in Virginia’s Allegheny Mountains, with a 50-acre lake.
evidence.quote: Douthat State Park is a state park located in the Allegheny Mountains in Virginia. It is in Bath County and Alleghany County. The park is 4,545 acres (18 km2) total with a 50-acre (20 ha) lake

evidence.claim: Many of its hiking trails originated with the Civilian Conservation Corps, which built the park in the 1930s.
evidence.quote: Over 43 miles (69 km) of varied difficulty trails are available, many of them created originally by the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.claim: Approximately 600 CCC men constructed most of the park between 1933 and 1942. One company handled forestry and trails, another the office, shelters and first 25 cabins, and a third the dam.
evidence.quote: Approximately 600 men from the Civilian Conservation Corps developed and constructed the majority of the modern-day park between 1933 and 1942.

evidence.claim: Douthat opened in 1936, but Virginia law excluded non-white visitors for its first 29 years.
evidence.quote: For the first 29 years Douthat was operational, Virginia state law barred non-whites from visiting Douthat State Park.

evidence.claim: The Clifton Forge NAACP pressed for an alternative for Black visitors, and Green Pastures Recreation Area opened in 1940. Virginia’s state parks ceased imposing segregation in 1965.
evidence.quote: In response, the Clifton Forge chapter of the NAACP lobbied for an alternate site for black citizens to visit, and the 133-acre Green Pastures Recreation Area was opened in 1940.

evidence.claim: One company handled forestry and trails, another the office, shelters and first 25 cabins, and a third the dam.
evidence.quote: Company 1836 conducted forestry work and trail construction, while Company 1374 constructed the original park office, shelters, beach complex building, and the initial 25 cabins. Company 1373 built the dam and spillway

evidence.claim: Douthat opened in 1936
evidence.quote: Douthat State Park opened on June 15, 1936

evidence.claim: Virginia’s state parks ceased imposing segregation in 1965.
evidence.quote: the Virginia state park system ceased imposing racial segregation in 1965.

evidence.claim: Longdale preserves a different transport connection: Longdale Station Road runs through a hamlet that once had a Chesapeake and Ohio railway station.
evidence.quote: It is placed near the North Mountain Subdivision of the Chesapeake and Ohio Railway. In the 19th century a station existed with the same name, and a road called Longdale Station (Virginia State Route 639) still runs through the hamlet.

evidence.claim: At Douthat Lake, Wilson Creek flows in from the mountains and continues below the dam’s spillway.
evidence.quote: Wilson Creek still flows down from the mountains and into Douthat Lake beside Lakeside Campground, and continues downstream of the dam's spillway.

evidence.claim: A change in locomotive technology shifted work away from Clifton Forge. The Chesapeake and Ohio railroad had established a major steam-engine maintenance facility here; during its heyday, the railroad employed over 2,000 people.
evidence.quote: The arrival of the Chesapeake and Ohio (C&O) railroad further grew the town, especially with the establishment of a major steam engine maintenance facility. During the railroad's heyday, it employed over 2,000 people.

evidence.claim: In the early 1950s, the company chose West Virginia for its diesel maintenance facilities, transferring many jobs there.
evidence.quote: In the early 1950s, the C&O decided to locate its diesel maintenance facilities in West Virginia, and many railroad jobs were transferred there.

evidence.claim: Railroad history remains a subject here through the Chesapeake & Ohio Historical Society and C&O Railway Heritage Center. The town also serves as a locomotive fueling location for CSX Transportation.
evidence.quote: Clifton Forge also serves a major locomotive fuel facility for CSX Transportation and is home to the Chesapeake & Ohio Historical Society and C&O Railway Heritage Center.

evidence.claim: Longdale Station Road carries a railway name through this Alleghany County hamlet. Longdale lies near the North Mountain Subdivision of the Chesapeake and Ohio Railway, and a station bearing the community’s name existed in the nineteenth century.
evidence.quote:
Longdale is an unincorporated community in Alleghany County, Virginia, United States.
It is placed near the North Mountain Subdivision of the Chesapeake and Ohio Railway. In the 19th century a station existed with the same name, and a road called Longdale Station (Virginia State Route 639) still runs through the hamlet.

evidence.claim: The road is numbered Virginia State Route 639. This is Longdale, distinct from the larger Longdale Furnace community to the east.
evidence.quote:
a road called Longdale Station (Virginia State Route 639) still runs through the hamlet.
The community is not to be confused with the larger Longdale Furnace to the east.

evidence.claim: Douthat Lake began with a dam across Wilson Creek. CCC Company 1373 built the dam and spillway, while other companies worked on the trails and park buildings.
evidence.quote: Company 1836 conducted forestry work and trail construction, while Company 1374 constructed the original park office, shelters, beach complex building, and the initial 25 cabins. Company 1373 built the dam and spillway, using Wilson Creek- the only natural body of water in the area- to create Douthat Lake.

evidence.claim: The resulting lake covers 50 acres.
evidence.quote: with a 50-acre (20 ha) lake

evidence.claim: Construction continued after the park opened on June 15, 1936, finally ending in 1942.
evidence.quote: Douthat State Park opened on June 15, 1936 alongside the other five original state parks in Virginia, all built with the men and resources of the Civilian Conservation Corps. Further work continued into 1941 and concluded in 1942

evidence.claim: Wilson Creek remains part of the lake’s geography: it descends from the mountains beside Lakeside Campground, enters the lake and continues downstream below the spillway.
evidence.quote: Wilson Creek still flows down from the mountains and into Douthat Lake beside Lakeside Campground, and continues downstream of the dam's spillway.

evidence.claim: Before the railroad expansion, the iron industry and a road over North Mountain had helped the settlement grow.
evidence.quote: The iron industry in the county and the completion of a road over North Mountain, now U.S. 60, caused the settlement to grow.

evidence.claim: The park’s three CCC companies divided the work: Company 1836 made trails and conducted forestry work, while Company 1374 built the first 25 cabins.
evidence.quote: Company 1836 conducted forestry work and trail construction, while Company 1374 constructed the original park office, shelters, beach complex building, and the initial 25 cabins.
